I. SOCIO/ECONOMIC CHARACTER
Implementation of the three-year Community Development Blocks Grant program will have a general positive impact on the social and economic impact of the target neighborhoods. Furthermore, the area-wide C.D.B.G. projects will have broader beneficial impacts on the community. The program, including the Housing Assistance Plan and the grant to the Housing Service Center, will help enable the city of San Jose to improve housing conditions and opportunities for the segment of the community which is elderly, lower income, Spanish-speaking or otherwise economically disadvantaged.
Although the C.D.B.G. program will not directly affect the standard socioeconomic indicators such as educational or income level, the program will have an overall positive impact by improving certain elements of the living environment for a large segment of San Jose's population.
J. COMMUNITY SERVICES AND FACILITIES
Implementation of the Community Development Block Grant program will not have any significant adverse impact on the availability or delivery of community services and facilities. Rather, the C.D.B.G. program will have a strong positive impact on the community. Since the demand for increased community services and the subsequent impact arises from increased population, the C.D.B.G. program will not have a noticeable effect. To a very marginal extent, the rehabilitation and improvements of the concerned neighborhoods will result in an increased local population. To the degree that this occurs, the demand for services in the Central and Alum Rock Planning Areas will be slightly increased. These areas are, however, in the city's Urban Service Area, within which the provision of services and facilities is most efficiently accomplished.
Municipal Water Supply
The proposed rehabilitation programs would not have a significant effect on the water system facilities of the City. Necessary relocations and adjustments would merely sustain the present level of operation. As a result of demolition, required local flows would be slightly and temporarily reduced.
Storm and Sanitary Sewers
The replacement of deteriorated sewer lines in Gardner and the installation of storm lines in Alviso will have a positive impact on those neighborhoods. Replacement of facilities will eliminate the leakage and infiltration problems, resulting in a more efficient sewerage system. There will be a minor and temporary reduction in sewerage flows as a result of demolitions and relocations.
